terms.p: The restriction that you may implement a trait for a type only if you defined the trait or you defined the type, so that no two crates can supply conflicting implementations.
A trait whose every method can be reached through a table of function pointers, which rules out generic methods, methods with no self, and methods returning Self by value.
The set of conditions a trait must meet before values of it can be used behind dyn, mainly that every method has a receiver and no type parameters of its own.
A trait named after a colon in another trait's declaration, meaning anything implementing the second must also implement the first.

terms.x: one type chosen by the implementor
terms.p: A type named inside a trait that each implementing type fixes exactly once, such as the Item an iterator yields.

terms.x: a trait method with a body
terms.p: A method written inside the trait itself in terms of the required ones, which every implementor receives for free and may override.

terms.x: an unnamed type meeting a bound
terms.p: Syntax standing for some single concrete type satisfying a trait, used as shorthand for a type parameter in an argument and to return a type that has no name.
